items.label: glamorous poem word
items.note: The word that sounds like it belongs in a poem is a reason to cut it; name a specific object.
items.negative: A kitchen with a cracked sink.

items.label: glamorous poem word
items.note: Say who spoke, how quietly, and what was said.

items.label: glamorous poem word
items.note: An echo is a stock effect; give the sound its source.

items.label: glamorous poem word
items.note: Break the thing in a specific way.

items.label: glamorous poem word
items.note: Things in poems dance too often; describe the movement.

items.label: named feeling
items.note: Withhold the emotion; show what the body or the room does.

items.label: named profundity
items.note: Silence as a noun of profundity is a ban-list word; say what is actually quiet.

items.label: announced significance
items.note: Do not announce that a moment matters.

items.label: simile
items.note: At most one simile in the poem; prefer describing the thing until it carries its own weight.

items.label: simile
items.note: A reflexive simile; cut it or keep it only if the poem cannot survive without it.
items.negative: As the room emptied, I left.

items.label: told emotion
items.note: Describe the chairs left behind and stop.

items.label: stock reaction
items.note: Let the reader supply the tears.

items.label: abstraction in place of an image
items.note: Name the thing the abstraction stands for.

items.label: archaic diction
items.note: Archaic words are a fingerprint of the borrowed poem; use the speaker's own.

items.label: stock ending
items.note: The sunset ending is the oldest closing image; find the one only this poem has.

items.pattern: \b(?:moon and june|heart and part|fire and desire|love and above)\b
items.label: stock rhyme
items.note: These pairs are decades worn; change one end word and the line it ends.
items.positive: her heart and part of mine
